words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) starts with the event of speaking before naming the speaker, so the intervention arrives first and is then assigned to {{ar:أَوْسَطُهُمْ}} ({{tr:awsaṭuhum}}). Its singular Form I perfect keeps this as one completed, direct act of saying, not collective speech, fabrication, or debate. The word also begins a speech-about-speech pattern: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) introduces the later {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}), so the present utterance recalls a previous warning and exposes the missing act of {{ar:تُسَبِّحُونَ}} ({{tr:tusabbiḥūna}}). Across the boundary from 68:27, the collective lament breaks into an individuated corrective voice; that single-voice warning pattern has useful parallels at 12:10 and 7:150, while the local point remains this speaker's confrontation of the group. The broader saying/glorification pairing is realized locally as speech diagnosing failed proper acknowledgment, with the cognate answer continuing in 68:29, and the q/l sound thread binds the saying verb, recalled saying, and addressed recipients into one audible reminder clause.

words.prose: {{ar:أَوْسَطُهُمْ}} ({{tr:awsaṭuhum}}) identifies the speaker as an internal member of the group, not as an outside commentator. The suffix binds him to them, while the elative form ranks him as the most centered or best balanced among them; the correction therefore rises from within the failed collective. Because this subject is revealed after the speech verb, the ayah first announces an intervention and then explains why this speaker matters. The word lets spatial middle and moral excellence work together: centeredness becomes the quality that authorizes the rebuke, with a mediating effect between group error and correction without turning the surface into a mediator noun. Its rare distribution and echo with the moderation vocabulary at 2:143 make the label load-bearing, but the local form remains a particular person in this parable, not a direct transfer of the community title. After the unified group speech of 68:27, the same group is now internally differentiated by a better-balanced witness in 68:28.

topics.reason: The construct-plus-suffix form makes the speaker one member among them, and the nominative phrase is the subject of {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}).

topics.reason: The afʿal elative and V4 branches support both centered position and choice justice; local speech context selects the moral-evaluative use without erasing the spatial image.

topics.reason: Mediation belongs to the root family, but the local word is the elative {{ar:أَوْسَط}} ({{tr:awsaṭ}}), so mediation is a role-effect of centered speech rather than the selected lexical noun.

words.prose: {{ar:أَلَمْ}} ({{tr:alam}}) fuses question and negation into the opening trigger of the rebuke. It governs {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}) as a jussive and turns the negative wording into an affirmative concession: the addressees are being made to admit that warning had already been given. Structurally it is the first beat of a two-step speech act, establishing prior warning before {{ar:لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ}} ({{tr:lawlā tusabbiḥūna}}) names the neglected glorification.

topics.reason: The particle complex combines interrogative force with negation over {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}), matching the input's rhetorical-question support.

words.prose: {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}) is the moderate speaker's first-person recalled saying, clipped into the jussive by {{ar:أَلَمْ}} ({{tr:alam}}). That form makes the prior warning grammatically dependent on the rhetorical question and personally accountable to the same speaker who now rebukes them. It also corrects the possible indexing confusion: in this frame the root is {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}), saying, not a fewness root. As the second q-w-l verb in the ayah, {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}) creates speech within speech: narrator report becomes quoted self-reference, and the remembered saying is paired with the failure to {{ar:تُسَبِّحُونَ}} ({{tr:tusabbiḥūna}}). Its clipped evidentiary recall also sets up the longer final reproach, so the pacing moves from proof of warning into the fuller charge.

topics.headline: the same speaker owns the prior warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker is not merely interpreting events afterward; he claims a prior warning that the group must now acknowledge.
topics.reason: The first-person singular agreement resolves to the speaker named in {{ar:أَوْسَطُهُمْ}} ({{tr:awsaṭuhum}}), and the utterance functions as a known question demanding concession.

topics.headline: the clipped form is governed recall

topics.reason: The jussive form results from governance by {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) inside {{ar:أَلَمْ}} ({{tr:alam}}).

words.prose: {{ar:لَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) fixes the warning's recipients before the ayah states the charge. With {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}), the prefixed lām selects the speech-recipient sense, so the phrase means that the warning was said to them, not merely for their benefit or possession. The attached plural pronoun keeps the garden owners personally addressed without renaming them, and its position before {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) makes accountability precede the demand for glorification.

words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) is the hinge from remembered warning to current charge. Because it is followed by the imperfect {{ar:تُسَبِّحُونَ}} ({{tr:tusabbiḥūna}}), it takes the taḥḍīḍ route, a reproachful "why did you not," rather than the obstacle-conditional route. The particle still carries a shade of regret or "if only" because the missing act is precisely what would have changed the scene, but local grammar keeps its function as direct exhortative blame. With no connector after {{ar:أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:alam aqul lakum}}), it fuses admission and charge into one escalating speech act.

topics.reason: The compound history and counterfactual adjacency are meaningful as semantic pressure, but the following imperfect prevents making a counterfactual conditional the local parse.

words.prose: {{ar:تُسَبِّحُونَ}} ({{tr:tusabbiḥūna}}) is the ayah's landing word and substantive charge. Its 2mp ending keeps the same addressees addressed in {{ar:لَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}), now recast as subjects of the neglected action. Under {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}), the indicative imperfect presents glorification as an ongoing practice they were failing to perform, not as a one-time jussive command. The object is unexpressed, so the act itself is foregrounded while the devotional object is recoverable from usage and from 68:29. The root's swimming and coursing image is narrowed by context into declaring divine transcendence: Form II turns motion pressure into repeated active acknowledgment rather than bare motion or inward self-devotion, and the doubled consonant audibly reinforces that intensity. Within the wider command and formula field visible at 56:74 and 56:96, this ayah invokes glorification by absence; the next ayah answers the missing verb with a cognate confession in 68:29. That forward turn changes the second-person charge into the group's response and makes the final verb a bridge from deprivation in 68:27 to confession in 68:29.

baseline_models.mechanism: The choice-balanced member converts an earlier utterance into preventive counsel: tasbih can encompass worship, thanks, and a God-willing exception, so the recalled speech was meant to qualify collective intention before its consequences arrived.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies both the original warning and its now-audible recall, making neglect rather than ignorance the issue.
Just and choice balance identifies the speaker as the member able to restrain an excessive collective intention.
Worship, thanks, remembrance, and God-willing exception make tasbih a practical qualification of action, not praise detached from it.

changed_reading.before: A generally better member scolds the others for failing to praise God.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant split mapping from qawl to fewness, not the ordinary sense of qala. It remains valid as a packet-supplied activation anchored in the repeated focus root and the central-position branch of awsat: a socially or numerically scarce warning can occupy structural center. Downstream prose should present it as a minority-voice image, never as a lexical claim that qala means few.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the cutting-in-half branch is form-distant from awsat as a person and the model is structural rather than lexical. It remains anchored in the focus middle and activated by the packet's repeated severance and bending images: the utterance interrupts a plan organized around a clean cut. Downstream prose should call it a counter-cut analogy, not translate awsat as cutter.

activation_trace.role: Cutting a thing into halves activates the middle speaker as the point where a unanimous plan can be interrupted.

Folding, bending, and turning supply the alternative geometry: exception bends the straight severing trajectory.

changed_reading.before: The person in the middle comments after the collective plan has failed.
changed_reading.after: The middle voice is an attempted counter-cut inside the plan, bending its drive toward total severance before consequence performs a harsher cut.

strongest_changes: Tasbih becomes the missing contingency that could have bent a collective oath away from total severance.
The immediate response performs tasbih as relocation of fault from the Lord to the group's own misplaced action.
The exclusion-deprivation reversal activates tasbih as keeping good and livelihood in circulation.
The later inability to submit turns the focus warning into a time-sensitive invitation while response remains possible.
summary.what_was_special: The focus sustained devotional, social-material, juridical, embodied, and kinetic readings at once. The strongest mechanisms did not collapse tasbih into one gloss, and the split qawl mapping plus the cutting branch of awsat preserved two contained readings a conservative synthesis would likely erase.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus may foreground God-willing exception, gratitude, purification of attribution, or all three without ranking them.
Awsat can support choice excellence, mediation, central position, or middling complicity; the packet does not force one social profile.
The circulation, kinetic, minority-voice, and counter-cut models are branch activations and should not be promoted into direct lexical translations.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The balanced member mediates interpretation.** `و س ط B001/B005` supplies just choice balance and mediation; repeated `ق و ل B001` frames his earlier and present speech. He stands linguistically between the group's first confusion and its confession. I infer balanced position -> capacity to mediate from event to responsibility; *awsaṭuhum* names a functional interpreter, not merely a spatial middle.
2. **Tasbih as the missing verbal restraint.** `س ب ح B001` includes worship, remembrance, thanks, and saying “if God wills”; `س ب ح B002` adds declaring free and distancing from wrong. Set against 68:18's failure to except, I infer tasbih would have interrupted absolute self-attribution and purified the plan of that claim. The question therefore recalls a practical corrective, not an ornamental formula.
3. **A prior saying returns as evidence.** The doubled saying activates `ق و ل B007/B015`, circulating report and earnest concern. His “did I not say” makes memory within the group part of the trial. I infer ignored counsel -> later evidentiary force; the ayah shows speech acquiring authority retrospectively through the event.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:29 immediately validates the mediator's diagnosis by eliciting *subḥāna rabbinā*, while 68:32 converts purified attribution into redirected desire. Later, 68:36's challenge to “how you judge” generalizes the need for a balanced interpreter.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The middle speaker as both balance and mediator.** Fixed `أَوْسَطُهُمْ` activates `و س ط B001` (just, choice balance) and `و س ط B005` (mediation between people). The group's hidden unanimity in 68:23, failed interpretation in 68:26-27, and mutual blame in 68:30 supply extremes needing reorientation; I infer that his position enables a corrective word to pass between collective resolve and collective collapse. “Middle” therefore names a functional social role, not only rank or location.
2. **Speech motivated by care and directed toward purification.** Fixed `قَالَ / أَقُل` activates `ق و ل B015` (earnest concern for something), while fixed `تُسَبِّحُونَ` activates `س ب ح B002` (purifying and declaring free). Their explicit purification of the Lord in 68:29 supplies the response; I infer that his prior warning seeks to separate divine agency from their corrupt plan and preserve the group from its result. The question reads as concerned intervention whose proposed mechanism is moral reattribution.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:29 directly fulfills the proposed purification, confirming fixed `تُسَبِّحُونَ` through `س ب ح B002`. 68:30's mutual blame then clarified why the fixed middle speaker also performs mediation (`و س ط B005`), not just balanced judgment.
